position.symbolic_location: Anonymous reconstructed roof in the South Division block bounded by Lake, Dearborn, Randolph and Clark; standing ON the Lake Street frontage itself, one unit of the party-line row along it
position.note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0078). This building does not stand centred on a lot at a typology setback: it stands ON the north face of blk_lake_clark, the block's Lake Street frontage, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is 0.80 m back from that lot line, which is NOT a measurement of this frontage either: it is the line the buildings already standing on this face were built to, adopted so that the face carries one street wall rather than two (T-0104). The plat module's lot margin still fixes the side lines this run stands clear of; what it does not fix is a street line that other records had already set, and its west wall is fixed by the east wall of recon_1835_blk_lake_clark_d3_02, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, so the front looks square at Lake Street. The run carries no lateral offset, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the 1834 South Water Street view supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous working row of party walls rather than detached cottages set back on grass. The treatment is what this placement takes from it, and a run standing on any other face of the town is borrowing it from that one street: the view draws a row, it does not place this row. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot, and the side lot lines this row crosses were always conjectural.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn from the set on this record's stable key, then advanced so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

occupants.note: SEATED BY THE STREET-FACE ADOPTION POLICY (docs/STREET-FACE-ADOPTION.md, the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 for T-0354, extended 2026-08-30 for T-0416; liberty L212). The newspaper register places this business on Lake Street AND NOTHING NARROWER — 2 printings, 1834-10-08 to 1834-11-12, claims chicago_democrat_1834_10_08#c004, chicago_democrat_1834_11_12#c012 — so it takes the STREET FACE and not a lot. THE ROOF'S PLATTED LOT FACES Lake Street, which is the plat's own answer to which street it fronts. WHICH roof on that face it is given is an allocation by tools/adopt_street_faces.py and not a reading of any source, and nothing here says this business stood nearer the corner than any other on the same face. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption: the business is documented, the building under it is not, and this attribute is graded `reconstructed` because the invented part is the whole of the placement.

frontage.why: T-0079, the third and last piece of the owner's flagged-important ask of 2026-08-18: "there should be more and denser buildings. this is important." THIS RUN IS THE DEMONSTRATION OF THE CORE DENSITY STANDARD and it is the first row in this project to stand three roofs on one lot. The old gate made a run carry exactly one roof per lot it was dealt, so this block's single free Lake lot could take a single cottage set back in the middle of it — which is the shape the owner's Tremont Street reference (data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md, image 5) is a picture of the town NOT having. The standard's ceiling is three units per lot, measured at the smallest lot on the committed grid, and this run spends all three. IT BUILDS TO THE CORNER, which is the clause of the standard no run could satisfy before it: anchored on the WEST end of its own frontage, the log dwelling's west wall stands 1.5 m from the Clark side line — the closest line the plat module's own margin allows — and the other two chain east off its wall in turn. WITHIN THE RUN THE END RULE ORDERS THEM, unchanged from every block of this row: better roofs nearer the town-centre end, which here is east toward Dearborn and the only crossing of the main stem in July 1835. So the log dwelling takes the Clark corner, the one-room cottage stands next to it and the deep-plan cottage closes the run at the east end, 10.58 m short of the bakery that already stands on the next lot. THIS RUN EXTENDS T-0077'S ROW ON THE SAME FACE: recon_1835_south_d3_013, inf_butcher_market, recon_1835_south_d4_014, recon_1835_south_d5_016 and recon_1835_south_c3_015 already stand shoulder to shoulder from 63.56 m to 97.57 m along this face, and inf_bakery_lake at 28.93 m to 34.49 m; the new run occupies 1.50 m to 18.36 m, so the Lake face of this block now carries built frontage at its west corner, its middle and its east end. NO COORDINATE IS AUTHORED HERE: the line, its bearing and the end the run packs away from are read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and the 1.5 m setback is the plat module's own lot margin rather than a measurement of this frontage.
